static-hosting.note: Served at <app>.proappstore.online over HTTPS from the platform host.

offline-pwa.note: A service worker is required of every app by the compliance check; the app template ships vite-plugin-pwa.

auth.limits: GitHub, Google, email + password; adult-provisioned login/password accounts for kids. Email magic-link is not enabled.

user-storage.limits: 64 KB per value, 1,000 keys and 10 MB per user per app

shared-data.limits: One SQL database (Cloudflare D1) per app, reached through up to 500 registered actions
shared-data.note: Reads and writes go through SQL actions declared in mcp.json, with per-action role gates.

counters.limits: 1,000 counters per app, key up to 128 chars, ±1,000 per increment

realtime.limits: 32 people per room, 4 KB per message, 100 messages/s; signed-in users only

file-storage.limits: 50 MB per file, 1,000 files per user per app in each area (private, public, review)

email.limits: 100 emails per app per day; 10 per recipient per day for user-to-user email
email.note: Only the app's owner or editors can send free-form email. Users can email other app members only through a fixed platform template. Nothing can send email on a schedule or from server code.

third-party-api-secret.limits: 5 secrets and 5 allowlisted hosts per app; 10,000 calls/day per app (1,000 per user); 100 KB request and response bodies; 30 s timeout
third-party-api-secret.note: Only signed-in users can call it, and only from the app's own origin in platform-cookie auth mode.

ai-user-key.note: There is no SDK helper. The app calls the provider directly from the browser, which the CSP allows (connect-src https:).

ai-platform.limits: Workers AI only (Llama 3.1 8B, Llama 3.3 70B, BGE embeddings); 200 units per user per day (70B costs 5); 20 calls/min; 1,024 max output tokens; 16,000-char prompt
ai-platform.note: The platform pays. Signed-in users only. No frontier models.

server-compute.note: App workers exist only as a prototype: at most 5 first-party apps (owned by a platform admin), enabled by an admin, and off in production. Every other app's deploy gets a 403.

scheduled-jobs.note: Schedules run only the app's own SQL actions (up to 5, every 5 minutes): they cannot fetch a URL or send push or email. Scheduled code needs an app worker, which only first-party apps can get.

payments.limits: Up to 20 products per app; one-off and subscription
payments.note: Checkout is refused for each app until a platform admin enables billing for it. Sales go through the platform's Stripe account; the revenue ledger records revenue but pays nothing out.

webhooks-out.limits: 10 webhooks per app; HMAC-SHA256 signed; HTTPS only
webhooks-out.note: Only three platform events: storage.uploaded, notification.sent and app.alert. An app cannot send webhooks for its own events.

webhooks-in.limits: 10 hooks per app, 5 MB body, 2,000 deliveries/day
webhooks-in.note: A verified hook (GitHub, Stripe, HMAC or token) can write its payload into the app's database through one SQL action. Sending a hook to custom code needs an app worker, which only first-party apps can get.

custom-domain.note: The owner can attach a domain, but it connects only if its DNS zone is in the platform's Cloudflare account. Domains with DNS elsewhere need Cloudflare for SaaS, which the platform owner has not enabled.

ads-free-tracking-free.note: PAS policy bans ads and trackers. Tracking SDKs fail a compliance check, which matches a fixed list of known trackers. Ads are banned by the guidelines only and nothing in code checks for them. Platform analytics are first-party and cookieless.

browser-geolocation.note: Foreground only; the browser asks the user.

browser-sensors.note: Accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer and ambient light. On iOS, DeviceMotionEvent.requestPermission() is needed.

browser-bluetooth-usb-serial.note: Allowed by the headers (bluetooth, usb, serial, hid), but Chromium browsers only.

browser-file-access.note: File pickers work everywhere. The File System Access API works in Chromium only.

browser-wasm.note: SharedArrayBuffer (threaded WASM) is opt-in per app with mcp.json "isolation", which turns on COOP/COEP.

browser-any-https-api.note: Any HTTPS or WSS endpoint and any HTTPS CDN script; plain http: is blocked. The target API must still allow CORS.

push-reminders.note: Nothing can send a push on a schedule: scheduled actions only run SQL and app workers have no push binding.

push-triggered.note: Web push works: users subscribe, the owner can broadcast from their own session, and users can notify each other. There are no scheduled or server-triggered pushes: scheduled actions only run SQL, and app workers have no push binding.

private-shared-data.limits: One SQL database per app, up to 500 declared actions
private-shared-data.note: Each read and write is a declared SQL action with its own role gate, so data can be private to a group (household, team, business and its customers).
